I'll agree that the deck design is degenerate, as are most one trick
ponies. But it is only a one trick pony (although it is a very nasty
trick). I am working with the idea that you're only going to get one
unblockable bleed per turn, if I am incorrect then I see it as more of a
problem with the rules that would allow Etrius to play RtI, be burned,
reappear and play another RtI (because it is a different Etrius), than the
cards. So unless I am completely missing a key element there are ways
around this blasted thing other than the ones mentioned above.

Is the player is so slick that no one is able to pummel Etrius into torpor
on their turns without burning him? (I have an old Soul Gem that requires
burning, so once again if this has been changed I am in error) Thus slowing
down the monstrosity.

And I don't know about everybody else but I see a well placed Pentax
Subversion as a big thorn in this deck's side. And it has become such a
useful card that we see them on quite a regular basis around here.

Both of the above will require the controller of Etrius to take the time to
influence a second copy of Etrius - - not much time if you are using ToR,
or if you are smart enough to start filling up a second copy of Etrius even
as the first one is still out. You are still talking about at least two
turns without a vampire once you bring the second copy of Etrius out to
contest the first.

Two turns without defense. If you survive, you have a very generous playing
circle.

Once again, I agree with you that the deck design is degenerate. But I
don't think that it is quite as unstoppable as is claimed, and I think that
a little more proof is going to be in order before WotC is going to feel
compelled to move on it. How often has this thing been played, or is it
merely theorectical? How often does it win? Does it sweep the table or
barely eek out a win? Does it have staying power or, does it need it? It
has no defense, does a heavy bleed preditor annihilate it before it even
gets out of the gates? Quite frankly if you play it without Adrian's
modifications I can see someone gaining a victory point and then suffering
the mother of all master hand jams on a regular basis.

And remember that every gaming circle will have different dynamics. Decks
like this one above have a nasty habit of dying very, very quickly in our
play circle.

Once again I will freely admit the possibility that I am working with some
flawed piece of knowledge here that will completely throw my arguement out
the window. I'm sure that soemone will kindly point it out to me if I am.
One thing to remember is that I am not LSJ or Adrian, I don't have their
ability to retain all of the current errata and rulings information. Though
it sure would be nice. :)

Messages.Author: PDB6
Messages.Body:
IMHO, Toomb of Ramses the Third is broken because it is a card that 99.9%
of all the decks in the game can benefit from having and the only reason
not to use it is because you don't own one. If I had a Tomb, I would put
it in every deck I have, as any deck, barring one that has a crypt of
exclusively 1-2 point vampires, will benefit from the Tomb.

Any card that will go in almost every deck you can possibly imagine, and
the only reason not to use it is that you don't own one (i.e. it is Rare),
is a broken card. Some examples from other games are:

-Magic's cheapie mana artifacts like Moxen and Lotai. All of these are in
EVERY winning type 1 deck. If you don't have them, you lose. The only
reason you don't use them is you don't own them.

-Legend of the Five Rings Inheritence and/or Imperial Gift. These are
both perfect examples of this sort of broken card. Without them, you are
at a great disadvantage, they go in EVERY deck, but as they are both Rare,
many people don't own them.

Tomb is the only card I can think of in all of Jyhad that fits this bill.
Even Wake With Evening Freshness, while arguably somewhat broken, does not
fit into these paramaters, as in many decks, WWEF will be just a waste of
deck space (only if adhereing to deck maximum sizes, though). The same
could be said for Info Super Highway, but again, it is easily omited from
many decks, and is only useful in the opening stages of the game (unless,
of course, you use it to get a greater benefit out of the Tomb :-). The
Tomb is always useful, and is worth getting out another vampire you have
no intention of bringing out just to use the Tomb.

While Tomb is in no way a game breaker in and of itself, it is a card that
will always pay back its intitial investment (and most of the time will
pay back in spades), has NO disadvantages (except its intitial cost of 3,
but the fact that there is no way to kill it the turn it is played insures
that the guy playing it will get 4 pool back that turn during influence),
will aid almost every deck in the game (except, again, an all weenie deck,
but even a deck like that can benefit from the Tomb as a constant Pool
income device, much like Eco Terrorists or Arcane Library), and is hard to
come by, as it is Rare. As a result of its scarcity, fewer people will
have it in their decks, and players who own a Tomb will have a definite
advantage over players who do not. This, to me, a broken card makes.

There could be many ways to fix this card, such as:

-Only works if you put the blood counters on the vampire with the Tomb.
This will slightly curtail the Blood Machine aspect of it.

-Needs to be tapped, and comes into play tapped. This will slow it down a
bit, and give other players a chance to destroy it before it pays for
itself.

-Disallow the removal of blood counters from the vampire with the Tomb.
This will shut down the Blood Machine aspect, but will still allow someone
to get out an IC member for free (well, the 3 for the Tomb, but that's
it).\

Messages.Author: PDB6

Randy wrote

"I still don't understand why it needs fixed."

Tomb needs to be fixed, simply, because it is too powerful. As I stated
in a very complete manner above, the Tomb is a card that provides a great
advantage without appreciable cost. One of the benchmarks of Jyhad is
that all cards have an appreciable cost. The Tomb costs 3 pool to play,
but as it cannot be destroyed the turn it is brought out, it will always
pay back 4 pool during influence. It has no disadvantages, and provides a
great advantage to a player who gets it out. It fits into every deck
design in the game. The ONLY reason not to put a Tomb in every deck you
own is that you don't have one. It is a card that is too powerful for
what it costs, has zero disadvantage, and is just plain wrong.

As LSJ pointed out above, a player used the Tomb at Gen Con to play 43
points of vampires for the cost of 3 pool. While this is an extreme
example, it is an example of what a sufficiently broken card can do.

My examples regarding possible fixes, such as making the Tomb start
tapped, were examples. In particular, making the Tomb start tapped would
allow other players a chance to kill it before it paid for itself, making
it risky to play it, as currently there is zero risk in playing it. All
other cards that have the potential to provide as much pool as the Tomb
are risky to play. For example, look at Blood Puppy or the Powerbases.
They can generate a great deal of pool for the guy who plays them, just
like the Tomb, but those cards are risky in that they can easily be killed
before they pay themself back or they can have all their pool stolen by
another player. The Tomb will ALWAYS pay for itself and has no built in
destruction clause, like both Blood Puppy and the Powerbases. The reason
that other master cards, like the Labyrinth or Blood Doll or Hunting
Grounds, should not come in tapped is that they are not broken cards. The
Tomb is a broken card, and thus somthing should be done to fix it, and if
it coming into play tapped fixes it, there you go.

The fact that the Tomb can be stopped by Sudden Reversal or Uniquness
simply does not fix it. The Tomb is something of a Trump card, as it
provides a great advantage with non appreciable cost. The fact that it is
Unique just reinforces it as a needed Trump card, as you need to have a
Tomb just in case your opponent has a Tomb. The only way to combat said
Trump is by using the same Trump. Thus there is an arms race of "who has
the Tomb", and the players without one will doubtlessly lose this arms
race.

Sudden Reversal kills any Master in the game, but the Tomb is the only
Master that is powerful enough to justify the inclusion of SR in every
deck you have, if for no other reason but to kill the Tomb. That, again,
begins an arms race that is fairly unprecidented in Jyhad. If a single
card (the Tomb) requires such a arms race, it is broken. There are no
other cards that do this. The Tomb does. It is just plain brown wrong.

The Tomb needs to be fixed. There could be many ways to fix it, as I
showed with multiple examples above, all of which would go some way twards
putting the card in line. As it is, it is not a huge game breaker, but is
too pwerful for what it costs and gives a great advantage to players who
own one, goes in EVERY deck, and the only reason not to use it is because
you don't own it.

I believe you're referring to my Inner Circle deck from GenCon.
The Tomb of Rameses III made that deck work. With the trim deck
size (60 cards), I had a reasonably good shot of getting an Info
Highway or a Tomb in the first draw. If I was lucky enough to get
the Tomb, then I would have two Inner Circle members out by the
end of my third turn. (Shudder.)

The deck used a blood gain strategy that relied on getting an Inner
Circle member out for almost nothing and then toasting them with Minion Tap/
Golconda/Redeem the Lost Soul for a preposterous blood pool gain.

Think about it: 3 pool with the Tomb to bring out Gwendolyn. Minion
tap for 10. Golconda for 11. Redeem for 5. That's a net gain of
23 pool.

All the deck had to do was oust its prey and then sit around gaining
blood. Once there were only two players left, I could smack my
prey with Return to Innocence and take home three victory points.

Sometimes (as in the Best of the Best tournament!) the deck could
get even more than 3 victory points.

Ultimately what made this deck work, however, was the Tomb of
Rameses III. If it's drawn early in the game, you use it to bring
out a huge vampire for 3 pool. If it's drawn late in the game, you
use it as a source of income. It always pays for itself on the
turn you bring it out.

The Tomb of Rameses III is a broken card.

BTW, I submitted the deck to the Corrupter. If he cares to post it,
you can see just how nasty this deck really is...

Messages.Author: David Hyatt
Messages.Body:
LSJ made the best point of all in this discussion. The Tomb pays
for itself IMMEDIATELY. There's no drawback. In one turn you get
(effectively) EIGHT transfers and gain a pool.

Another interesting pattern I've seen in games with lots of Tombs...
people frequently don't contest the Tomb, because they know it will go
away in only a turn or two anyway. Then they can play their Tomb and
reap the full benefits without paying the cost of contesting.

My proposal for fixing the Tomb:
Have the blood from the Tomb placed ON the Tomb and NOT on the
vampire. With this modification, you can't pull blood off the
Tomb, so it can't be used as a source of income. If the Tomb
gets burned then you'll lose the blood on the Tomb. Only if the
blood on the Tomb + the blood on the vampire = the blood capacity
of the vamp do they come into play. Also that gives other players
the opportunity to burn or contest the Tomb BEFORE the player really
gains any benefit from the card.

Anyway, the Corrupter mailed me my deck submission, since I took
the deck apart after GenCon (I made a vow never to play the deck
again!). Here it is:

Meet the Inner Circle
Environment: Take your pick
Commentary: This deck is designed to get 3 victory points. It is
first and foremost a blood-gaining machine. Use the minion taps,
blood dolls, and tombs to gain blood. Use the Golconda/Redeem the
Lost soul combo for another big blood boost. The idea behind this
deck is to oust your prey as quickly as possible. Oust others if
the opportunities present themselves. Otherwise, hang out, gain
pool, and wait until it comes down to you and one other person.
Then cash in the Return to Innocence and take the last two victory
points.

Messages.Author: Thomas Doehne
Messages.Body:
I agree, the Tomb is broken, and needs to be fixed. Following on
Peter's comparison to Blood Puppy and Powerbases, I'd make two
fixes:

1. Blood is moved onto the Tomb, not the vampire. The Tomb can
be burned (and the blood moved to the vampire) to bring a
vampire into the ready region.

This change removes the 'perpetual blood supply' aspect of
the tomb.

2. Blood can be stolen from the Tomb with a directed action,
at no stealth.

I'm not sure this change is needed, if the first is made.

--
Tom Doehne
doe...@cse.ogi.edu

Messages.Author: Thomas Doehne
Messages.Body:
In article <5333rc$cno...@leeds.ac.uk> GEN...@leeds.ac.uk

(B.D. Redmond) writes:
>In article <52r949$g...@news.cais.com>, cbo...@apdi.net (Sorrow) wrote:

[other commentary about the Tomb omitted].

>We also see no problem with the tomb - apart from its lack of any alignment
>to clan, its a poor arcane library/Eco terrorists/art museum. under a card
>limit environment it doesn't seem to cause a problem - even if it has used
>in a lot of decks, it doesn't spoil the game.

It's far superior to the Arcan/Eco/Art Museum cards. It gives you
more free pool a turn, since you can keep sucking blood off almost
indefinitely. With Information Highway, it can give you 2 pool
a turn. But that's not the worst. Worst is the ability to get
a big vampire out very, very fast, for no cost but the 3. Then
Minion Tap, Golconda, rinse, repeat.

Of course it's no problem under CL. Instead of having problems with
individual cards, you have:
1. Domination of the game by Malkavian Sneak and Bleed (and now
probably Setite Sneak and Bleed).

2. Evisceration of numerous competing strategies:
Ways of dealing with S&B
-- Rush combat: no longer effective, since you can't put
enough get-in-combat cards in the deck.
-- Bleed bounce, except for Tremere and Malks, since you
can't put enough bounce cards in your deck
Ways of dealing with combat:
-- Run-away combat, for clans without celerity.
Offensive strategies
--Rush combat: As above, not enough get-in-combat cards.
--'Pitch' combat decks: can't put in enough maneuvers or
enough long-range combat cards to be effective.
--Voting: A limited number of damaging vote cards. Especially
if you want to play Presence voting, rather than Princely vote,
since you can't use Parity Shift or Sabbat Threat. Presence voting
also gets hosed because you have only 4 Bewitching Orations and
4 Bribes, both necessary to help get those votes passed.
-- Tap-and-Vote/Bleed. These rely heavily on the combat
untap cards, Majesty/Earth Meld, to tap out the prey. With
only four, you can't make it work.

3. Rare cards become more valuable.
Since you can only have a limited number of each card, the
rare stand-ins become much more valuable: Fists of Death
in place of Torn Signpost and Undead Strength, Kine
Dominance in place of Govern the Unaligned, etc. This
favors Mr. Suitcase over the beginning player, a bad thing
IMO.

4. Because S&B is dominant, everyone ends up playing intercept.
This slows the game down a lot. Also a bad thing, IMO.

Standard responses to CL arguments:
1. If you have a jerk playing Sneak & Bleed, just
gang up, or use social pressure to make them quit.

Answer: If you have to resort to the metagame of social
pressure or ganging up, the game is broken. Most of us
would rather it worked without having to resort to this.
And NL/Golden Tenets does.

2. CL is more creative, because you have to be more inventive
in combining cards.

Answer: CL shuts off a *lot* of otherwise effective strategies.
What you're doing is agreeing to play with relatively ineffective
decks. The game's not broken, so you don't need to do this.
(As long as you use the Golden Tenets.) Basically, any
deck you can build under CL you can use under NL. And under
NL, you don't have to rely on intercept for defense, which
lets you be more creative, not less.

3. Well, we just play for fun. CL is better for that.

Answer: So do NL players. The range of possible decks
is much wider under NL. Voting and rush combat are now
workable deck concepts. The games are quicker. And you
don't have to wean new players off of Sneak & Bleed to
preserve balance. We'll just have to agree to disagree
about which is more fun.

4. We don't have to worry about broken cards.

Answer: Well, then the game becomes more like Magic --
whoever draws their broken cards first wins. We don't
really want that kind of a game, do we? But yes,
you don't have to worry as much about them.

There have been few broken cards, and they have been
fixed by errata or the Golden Tenets. Those methods
are far preferable to the Procrustean bed of Card Limits.

I hope that this will speed the debate up a bit.

--
Tom Doehne

Many argue that Golden Tenets do the same to Tap-and-XXX decks. For an

> This slows the game down a lot. Also a bad thing, IMO.

Many argue that intercept in every deck is a useful thing. I also
disagree, mostly on the grounds that there are always other options.
While intercept is often and usually useful, that doesn't mean it belongs
in most decks.

> Standard responses to CL arguments:
> 1. If you have a jerk playing Sneak & Bleed, just

> Answer: If you have to resort to the metagame of social
> pressure or ganging up, the game is broken. Most of us

That it does (with the notable exception of the Return to Innocence deck.
Design Team? Are you listening?)

[snipped answers to CL arguements about creativity, fun games]

> Answer: Well, then the game becomes more like Magic --
> whoever draws their broken cards first wins. We don't
> really want that kind of a game, do we? But yes,
> you don't have to worry as much about them.

EXACTLY. One of the many reasons I prefer Jyhad is that it relies more on
deck design and less on luck (and wealth). While it _is_ a card game and
therefore subject to luck, because there is no arbitrary limit to the
numbers of cards played, deck design creates your own luck, rather than

> There have been few broken cards, and they have been
> fixed by errata or the Golden Tenets. Those methods
> are far preferable to the Procrustean bed of Card Limits.

> I hope that this will speed the debate up a bit.

That would be nice.

This fix for the Tomb is very good. What it reduces the
Tomb to is a non-immediate blood gainer in the later game, and is
a more reasonable card in the beginning of the game.

> 2. Blood can be stolen from the Tomb with a directed action,
> at no stealth.
> I'm not sure this change is needed, if the first is made.

In my playgroup, Powerbase:Blood Gain are rarely, if ever,
seen. The only one I've ever seen in actual play was P:Chicago, and
no one ever put more than one blood on it at a time. They aren't
as cost-effective as Short Term Investments, and you really have to
be playing an intercept-combat deck to use them well. Reducing the
Tomb of Ramses to the power of Powerbase: Washington, D.C., would be
too much.
Disputed Territory on the New Tomb would be very fair. Just
be careful about when the Tomb can be burned.

-Nathan Harada

Definitely _more_ reasonable(how could it be any less?) But, still broken
in terms of the ability to pull out a larger vampire for less pool at high
speed. This one would be fine if the tomb was recosted to, say, 4 or 5
pool. Also, it should be something along the lines of "all blood
transferred onto _This_ vampire." Maybe that's a little bit harsh.

Hmm... How about keep it as is(beyond uping the cost) but no transfers
can be made to or from the vampire with the tomb on him or her? That will
take down the speed aspect, and although it'll still be overpowered, it
won't take the cake like it does now.

I still think that multiple fixes should be applied, so it gives either
a) speed, but no or not much net gain in pool, and only for the largest
vampires;
or
b) efficiency in transfers, (but not too much efficiency) but no speed
boost(heck, we've already got Info Highway, guys).

Agreed. The only use for Powerbase: Washington D.C. we thought up would
be a guy with a Succubus club trading it with a truly intimidating
intercept deck, and then taking the D action to take the blood off without
being blocked. The intercept deck would get the same deal with the
Succubus club guy when the Powerbase was traded back.

> Disputed Territory on the New Tomb would be very fair. Just
> be careful about when the Tomb can be burned.

The burn fix is IMHO, overused, and probably too much of a weakness. Is
it just me, or does the profusion of "Burn this card as a D action" stilt
the game towards intercept combat even more than it was already?

Alec Chang

Speed and Efficiency of Pool are what the tomb currently grants.
Take away one of them, and It'll become less overpowered and become

4 capacity, I put it in my deck."

The problem with this(not that I think that it's a bad idea)
is that people will have to consider the contingency of their opponents
playing with tombs, and have to pack cards which burn or steal it
PRIMARILY for the tomb, and only secondarily for other effects.



could get even more unpleasant if it was focusing on using one or
two of the included strategies to oust people. If it packed multiple
RTI's, w/ day ops or just the stealth to avoid being blocked, it would
be terrifying. With more Anarch Revolts, the same can be said. More
Damage-dealing votes; same thing. If the designer was actively
_trying_ to make it less pleasant, it wouldn't take much more effort.

Does anyone else see this? A broken card made this possible; and more
ordinary or broken cards mixed in would make it even more deadly
than it is right now.

Alec Chang

Messages.Author: B.D. Redmond
Messages.Body:
Tomb of Ramses III is *****NOT***** too powerful by any means. Lets start by
examining the arguments that claim the contrary.

1: ToR is too powerful because all decks will put on in their deck.

- why does this make it too powerful? Surely an essential game balancing
aspect of Jhyhad / V:tES is that certain defensive cards (such as Sudden
reversal and Wakes) and blood back cards (such as blood dolls and
investments) have always been open for everyone to use to stop various clans
from being too much harder than any others. ToR is just another blood back
card that can be used by any clan. The fact that it is unique makes it even
less game destroying by everyone having out three or four of them. To all
the people out there who believe in the original argument that ToR is too
powerful as all decks will use it, I put it to you that you are just pissed
off that someone else invarably got it out before you and you couldn't get
yours out.

2: ToR is too powerful because it gets you back four blood from the blood
bank in the turn it comes out.

- Okay, perhaps this is a much more reasonable argument, however this blood
gain nets at one. How many other ways are there for gaining you one blood?
it must be heading towards tripple figures, if not there already.

3: Tor is too powerful because it gives you an endless blood supply.

- So do three other cards, although they are clan specific, they are
arguably twice as good. ToR, used as a blood gainer gets back 2 blood every
3 turns for a three blood down payment, the others get you 1 per turn for a
2 pool cost.

QED

Messages.Author: L. Scott Johnson
Messages.Body:
GEN...@leeds.ac.uk (B.D. Redmond) writes:
>Tomb of Ramses III is *****NOT***** too powerful by any means. Lets start by
>examining the arguments that claim the contrary.

You missed one.

4. TOR is too powerful because it gives you a large capacity vampire for
free with almost no defense possible (and the only "defenses" merely
curtail the usefulness - the defenses will never wind up as a net loss
for the person playing TOR).

The only defenses to TOR are Arson, Rampage, Disputed Location, and
Kine Dominance (Dominate Kine). - All of these are of limited usefulness
in that they don't directly benefit the person playing them, and the
target has already netted at least one pool by the time she loses the TOR.

If you fail to get the Arson/Rampage/DL/KD in your hand in time (<3 turns),
then it will be useless. Even if you get it, it can still be easily
blocked (Arson/Rampage), or possibly defeated (DL). The best chance
costs your vampire two blood and is a rare.

Whoever gets the Tomb out first wins a large percentage of the time
(at least in our playgroup).

That's the essence of a broken card.

Messages.Author: theCorrupter
Messages.Body:
On Mon, 7 Oct 1996, B.D. Redmond wrote:

> Tomb of Ramses III is *****NOT***** too powerful by any means. Lets start by
> examining the arguments that claim the contrary.

And let's responding by destroying your own.

> 1: ToR is too powerful because all decks will put on in their deck.

[snipped response to this "arguement"]

Suffice it to say, people aren't saying that ToR is powerful because
people are putting it in their deck, they _are_ saying that it is too
powerful, and that people putting it in their deck is a symptom of its
power. Do note, that useful cards are also put into most decks (Blood
Dolls, Wakes), though not all, but that the argument was _not_ claiming
this use = power, but that power = use. (Sorry to be redundant)

> 2: ToR is too powerful because it gets you back four blood from the blood
> bank in the turn it comes out.

> - Okay, perhaps this is a much more reasonable argument, however this blood
> gain nets at one. How many other ways are there for gaining you one blood?
> it must be heading towards tripple figures, if not there already.

That's not the full argument. To take this aspect of the argument out of
context is misleading. The full argument is that it is powerful in its
own right, but that there is _no_ drawback to its use. The turn it is
brought out, you can get return on it. Effectively, you pay _ONE_ master
phase for an ascendance _AND_ its power.

If the card stalled somehow (not usable during the first turn, for
example), there would be a risk element involved in its use. As it
stands, you can only gain if you have one in a deck (in _nearly_ all
situations).

> 3: Tor is too powerful because it gives you an endless blood supply.

> - So do three other cards, although they are clan specific, they are
> arguably twice as good. ToR, used as a blood gainer gets back 2 blood every
> 3 turns for a three blood down payment, the others get you 1 per turn for a
> 2 pool cost.

This is only if the vampire who has the tomb on it is not used as a
resource. Assuming a large vampire (say, 10 capacity), a first turn tomb
of ra nets you 1 pool the first turn, 4 pool the next, and 2 pool the
last. Effectively, you gain 7 pool over three turns, and get _DOUBLE_
influence. All for 3 pool. Come on! Even if the Tomb is Destroyed, the
gain made so far is not lost. There needs to be some risk factor.

Yes, if used solely in late game as a pool feeder (Tomb on, transfer off),
it is not as effective as say an Arcane Library, but the fact that it can
be used for this, as well as the above, makes it too cheap.

Messages.Author: Thomas Doehne
Messages.Body:
In article <53b0l7$djc...@leeds.ac.uk> GEN...@leeds.ac.uk

(B.D. Redmond) writes:
>Tomb of Ramses III is *****NOT***** too powerful by any means. Lets start by

>

>1: ToR is too powerful because all decks will put on in their deck.
>

> - why does this make it too powerful? Surely an essential game balancing

>reversal and Wakes) and blood back cards (such as blood dolls and
>investments) have always been open for everyone to use to stop various clans
>from being too much harder than any others.

However, the cards *everyone* uses are commons. ToR is rare. It's a
lot more like a Lotus than any other card in the set.

>2: ToR is too powerful because it gets you back four blood from the blood
>bank in the turn it comes out.

> - Okay, perhaps this is a much more reasonable argument, however this blood
>gain nets at one. How many other ways are there for gaining you one blood?
>it must be heading towards tripple figures, if not there already.

If this was all it did, it would be just fine. But it does a lot more --
see below.

>3: Tor is too powerful because it gives you an endless blood supply.

> - So do three other cards, although they are clan specific, they are
>arguably twice as good. ToR, used as a blood gainer gets back 2 blood every
>3 turns for a three blood down payment, the others get you 1 per turn for a
>2 pool cost.

Tomb of Ramses has two effects:
1. It gives you, in effect, *four* free transfers. Sure, it
might go away, but it is already superior to the Information
Highway just on this basis alone. And Info Highway is
itself a very useful and much-contested card.

2. It gives you up to four free pool a turn. Much better than
any other blood gaining card. The only other one that lets you
show a profit on the turn you play it is Ascendance. Let's
compare it to Short Term Investment:
First Turn: STI, net 0 Tomb: net 1
Second STI, net 1 Tomb: net 5
Third STI, net 3 Tomb: net 9 (if it hasn't been used up already).
*And*, those gains don't require a master phase, unlike
STI, PI, nad Ascendance

3. Compare to the Ecoterrorists/Art Museum/Arcane Library:
It shows a profit on the first turn, they don't.
It gives you *four* free transfers a turn, rather than 1.

It's better than having both Ecoterrorists *and* Info
Highway out. Any card that's better than a combination
of two of the better cards in the game is very, very
good.

--
Tom Doehne
doe...@cse.ogi.edu

>After a few games getting blasted they will probably quit running a
>degenerate deck. If they don't they will continue to get blasted and
>probably quit playing with you. This will also solve the problem.

This solves the problem, but only in isolated game groups. Whenever you
have significant turnover, or play with other groups, or have visitors
this won't work.

The real killer for social solutions is that a popular game, like chess,
bridge, or (sigh) Magic, is characterized by playing in large variable
groups and with strangers. If Jyhad is successful, it will be popular,
and then you necessarily have a situation where social controls don't
work.

well, actually this fact has been covered in two of my other arguments in
the original post, but if you need two and two added together for you, here
goes....

FREE????? okay, lets say you have a ten (or eleven, for that matter) blood
vampire in your crypt. you put ToR (Tomb of Ramses III) on it before you
have put any blood on it. ToR costs three blood to get out, and doubles up
the blood that you have put on it with transfers. so, a ten blood vampire
gets up to eight blood in one turn and comes out in the next. You have put a
total of five blood on it and gained five from it. However - the tomb has
cost you three. That gives you a maximum net gain of 2 - the same as a short
term investment (Okay so its quicker, but the short term was shit anyway).
the other argument here is that the vamp gets out quickly as well. However
this is no quicker to other similar cards: Information highway (IH), Art
museum et al (AMea). The IH is different in that it does not give you any
blood back, however, how and where you spend the additional influence it
gives you and the fact that it isn't burnt when the vampire comes out makes
it a far less restrictive card, and for the blood price is fairly well
balanced with ToR. AMea also allows you to get a ten blood vampire out in
two turns, however you will have less influence left after this, and will
have not netted any blood gain yet, however, it takes just two turns to
to net the same gain, and you can carry on gaining blood for the rest of the
game. ToR is, as was designed (I presume), to be an inferior AMea, but that
anyone can use - which can actually work against it as it is more likely to
be contested. I think that sums it all up.

>The only defenses to TOR are Arson, Rampage, Disputed Location, and
>Kine Dominance (Dominate Kine).

Disputed location???? surely you mean disputed territory. You should
perhaps also add sudden reversal and unnatural disaster (see below).

> - All of these are of limited usefulness
>in that they don't directly benefit the person playing them,

Excuse me? I beg your pardon? Disputed territory and Kine dominance don't
benefit the person playing them directly? So, you think that ToR is too
good, and in that case you don't think that it would be beneficial to you to
control it yourself instead? I think your logic is very strange on this
account. As for the others, if you think that ToR is so powerful, whats
wrong with spending an mere action to prevent someone from having it?

> and the target has already netted at least one pool by the time she loses
>the TOR.

Read my other post - there are many other ways to net yourself one blood -
one of which is to get out a caitiff and bleed someone who hasn't got out
any Vamps because he's plying all his efforts into the ToR! Don't stress
about a measly one blood anyway. WOW! all bow down and praise the methusulah
who has managed to gain ONE BLOOD!!!!

>If you fail to get the Arson/Rampage/DL/KD in your hand in time (<3 turns),
>then it will be useless.

Okay, but so then will be the ToR and they will have only gained two blood
from it, If you do the caitiff method suggested above you can gain more than
this before anyone gets into a situation where they can gain the edge back
from you, Hunting grounds and AMea are equally good at gaining you far more
blood than the ToR, although slightly slower, but lets face it, what gamne
only lasts 5 rounds (after which you would have netted the same gain as the
ToR).

>Even if you get it <Counter card>, it can still be easily

>blocked (Arson/Rampage), or possibly defeated (DL). The best chance
>costs your vampire two blood and is a rare.

Possibly, but if the Person with ToR is too busy plying all his available
resources into the ToR then they won't have anyone out to block, will
they.... Also, ever heard of stealth??? Kine Dominance is still a Zero
stealth action and so is just as easily blocked as Arson or rampage, as for
the blood cost - I think its worth two blood off one of my vampires for a
three blood location. Rarity noted and accepted. For a voting deck Disputed
Territory is by far the best option (lets face it, a vote deck without these
is stabbing itself in the foot), its at +1 stealth, and early on in the game
a vote can be won on the strength of the +1 vote the card gives you alone.
Sudden reversal is a very good counter to anything, and you are likely to
have as many SRs as your opponent will have ToR's, so its merely a matter of
luck as to who get what out when etc. Finally, unnatural disaster.... okay
so its not brilliant but its safe - the only counter is SR, which means that
you don't loose the pool; played early on it can be a very useful card.

>Whoever gets the Tomb out first wins a large percentage of the time
>(at least in our playgroup).

Perhaps you should all start to make better decks then, in our play group, I
took it out of my deck because it wasn't good enough at getting me blood
back.

>That's the essence of a broken card.

Then I think you should stop playing, because there are many cards as
powerful, if not more powerful, the ToR, and they are all likely to stop you
from enjoying yourself because your deck just isn't good enough to cope with
the above averege cards.

*other* vampires.

>gets up to eight blood in one turn and comes out in the next. You have put a
>total of five blood on it and gained five from it. However - the tomb has
>cost you three. That gives you a maximum net gain of 2 - the same as a short
>term investment (Okay so its quicker, but the short term was shit anyway).

Actually, for the 11-cap, you get a maximum net gain of eight - 11
matched by the TOR, minus the three the TOR cost to play. It'd take
a lot more time and cards to get the same benefit from any Investments.

>the other argument here is that the vamp gets out quickly as well. However

>[... other speedy examples deleted ...]

Speed wasn't part of my Argument.

>>The only defenses to TOR are Arson, Rampage, Disputed Location, and
>>Kine Dominance (Dominate Kine).

>Disputed location???? surely you mean disputed territory. You should

Surely, I do, of course.

>perhaps also add sudden reversal and unnatural disaster (see below).

SR - yes. UD - no. Spending two pool after the TOR has already netted
the person playing it a pool isn't a good defense. Even with the SR,
the person playing TOR hasn't lost anything more than you. The TOR
is without drawbacks.

>> - All of these are of limited usefulness
>>in that they don't directly benefit the person playing them,

>Excuse me? I beg your pardon? Disputed territory and Kine dominance don't
>benefit the person playing them directly? So, you think that ToR is too
>good, and in that case you don't think that it would be beneficial to you to
>control it yourself instead? I think your logic is very strange on this
>account. As for the others, if you think that ToR is so powerful, whats
>wrong with spending an mere action to prevent someone from having it?

You are excused. Read the card. Changing the controller doesn't allow
you to change the target. If you steal it, it either won't have a target
at all, or will still target the original vampire (probably the latter,
by card text, but that's up to the RT to decide in their next meeting :-)

>> and the target has already netted at least one pool by the time she loses
>>the TOR.

>Read my other post - there are many other ways to net yourself one blood -

Read the other posts here. The one blood gain isn't the end - it's just
the worst case scenario. The point her is that there is no risk involved
in playing TOR - your get your cost back, plus interest (one pool) before
anyone can do anything about it. *Then*, it continues to provide it's
benefit until it is stolen/burned.

(The only possible way to lose with the TOR is if someone already has
the Madness Network out and steals/destroys the Tomb at the end of your
minion phase - not very likely, and if the MNet is out, you can just wait
until the Malks are tapped)

>>If you fail to get the Arson/Rampage/DL/KD in your hand in time (<3 turns),
>>then it will be useless.

>Okay, but so then will be the ToR and they will have only gained two blood
>from it,

Eight, not two.

>>Even if you get it <Counter card>, it can still be easily
>>blocked (Arson/Rampage), or possibly defeated (DL). The best chance
>>costs your vampire two blood and is a rare.

>Possibly, but if the Person with ToR is too busy plying all his available
>resources into the ToR then they won't have anyone out to block, will

What "all resources"? You play the card, reap the reward (one pool)
immediately, then continue for as long as you have it. There is no
required resource expenditure after the fact.

>they.... Also, ever heard of stealth??? Kine Dominance is still a Zero
>stealth action and so is just as easily blocked as Arson or rampage, as for
>the blood cost - I think its worth two blood off one of my vampires for a
>three blood location. Rarity noted and accepted. For a voting deck Disputed
>Territory is by far the best option (lets face it, a vote deck without these
>is stabbing itself in the foot), its at +1 stealth, and early on in the game
>a vote can be won on the strength of the +1 vote the card gives you alone.

Sure. And, as I said - all of those will be too late to actually *cost*
the person with the TOR any net loss.

>Sudden reversal is a very good counter to anything, and you are likely to
>have as many SRs as your opponent will have ToR's, so its merely a matter of
>luck as to who get what out when etc. Finally, unnatural disaster.... okay

And, even with SR, there's no net loss between the two of you.

>so its not brilliant but its safe - the only counter is SR, which means that
>you don't loose the pool; played early on it can be a very useful card.

And, with the Disaster, you have a net three pool deficit (TOR gained
one the same turn - you spent two to prevent further gain).

>>Whoever gets the Tomb out first wins a large percentage of the time
>>(at least in our playgroup).

>Perhaps you should all start to make better decks then, in our play group, I
>took it out of my deck because it wasn't good enough at getting me blood
>back.

Perhaps you should try playing the TOR to its full potential (gaining
eight instead of two might make for a different game).

>>That's the essence of a broken card.

>Then I think you should stop playing, because there are many cards as
>powerful, if not more powerful, the ToR, and they are all likely to stop you
>from enjoying yourself because your deck just isn't good enough to cope with
>the above averege cards.

Such as...

Messages.Author: B.D. Redmond
Messages.Body:
In article <533rv9$2...@reuter.cse.ogi.edu>,

>
>>We also see no problem with the tomb - apart from its lack of any
>>alignment to clan, its a poor arcane library/Eco terrorists/art museum.
>>under a card limit environment it doesn't seem to cause a problem - even
>>if it has used in a lot of decks, it doesn't spoil the game.
>
>It's far superior to the Arcan/Eco/Art Museum cards. It gives you
>more free pool a turn, since you can keep sucking blood off almost
>indefinitely.

Here I think that you will find that you are wrong. If you are going to use
ToR as a continal blood flow it gives you **less** blood per turn than the
Art Museum et al (AMea). Lets establish the facts shall we?
1: AMea gives you one blood back a turn at the cost of two
transfers.Surely no one can argue with that?
2: ToR, at best, gives you back four blood every five turns,
at the cost of all four transfers. Lets examine how exactly
this is done, shall we?
i) you spend all four transfers and stick on four
blood. ToR doubles this to eight.
ii) You take off two per turn each turn thereafter,
meaning that
after five turns you have gained four blood, in the same
time AMea would have gaied you 5 blood. Including the cost
to bring it into play, after five turns ToR has netted you 1
pool and the AMea 3 pool.

There are other reasons why AMea is better than the ToR. They are as
follows:
1: ToR costs three pool to bring out, AMea costs two, thereby
meaning that AMea cards can be played as a last minute
defense to gain you the blood to keep you in, where as ToR
takes longer to reqoup itself back into your pool.
2: if used as a continual blood gaining card ToR ties up one
vampire for the entire game and the ToR is only at its most
efficient if that vampire is 5 (not much use to a weenie
deck) capacity or higher. AMea cards, although requiring a
specific vampire clan, are not as restictive as ToR, you may
place blood continually, and choose to bring out or keep
back vampires as you see fit.

>With Information Highway (IH), it can give you 2 pool a turn.

lets take the same situation - put on six blood - twelve blood is present
on your vampires. if you take it of at a rate of three a turn, in four
more turns you will have gained six blood from the ToR. This nets, in five
turns as +3 pool, which is the same as the AMea. Accepted, in the long run
it will be slightly better, gaining you six blood every five turns rather
than the five the AMea gets you - but if its not destroyed in five turns the
decks your playing against just aren't that good. Even still, this is a two
master card combo and would be dificult to get out, especially with both of
these cards beeing some of the rarer uncommons (I'm the only one in our
group who has got an Info Highway out of a packet, no one has more than one
ToR or IH).

>Of course it's no problem under CL. Instead of having problems with
>individual cards, you have:

>1. Domination of the game by Malkavian Sneak and Bleed (and now

>probably Setite Sneak and Bleed).

Wrong, no one plays S&B, because its boring as hell and spoils the game for
everyone - there's no challenge to winning with a S&B deck, and it has also
become equally easy to loose with one - its all down to the luck of the card
spread. WOW thats exciting!!! Also the permanents based enviroment CL tends
to generate make S&B less powerful, especially with Heidelburg.

>2. Evisceration of numerous competing strategies:
>Ways of dealing with S&B
> -- Rush combat: no longer effective, since you can't put
> enough get-in-combat cards in the deck.

wrong. you just have to be clever about it - use more permanent and semi
permanent rush - makesure that when you do use rush it counts, theres no
problem of rush hand jam under CL.

> -- Bleed bounce, except for Tremere and Malks, since you
> can't put enough bounce cards in your deck

You've got as many as your predator has bleed modifiers, normally. If not
its a case of making them count. AI means that no one risks a bleed of three
or more, so telepathic counter becomes useful too. using two clan decks, or
common secondary skills with skill card bonuses in there makes Toreador and
ventrue and giovanni readonable - even nosferatu, brujah and gangrel could
get out one vampire to act as a bleed bouncer. But then, if no one is
playing S&B, theres no real need for a deck solely devoted to bleed bounce.

>Ways of dealing with combat:
> -- Run-away combat, for clans without celerity.

I have had many succesful ranged combat decks. Protean is almost as good at
getting to range, as is thaumaturgy. Fortitude can get you there also (if
you really need to), as can obfuscate, serpentis, animalism, auspex and
potence. Its just a case of being prepared and using the cards you have
available to you to their best capacity. And *then* theres fake out.
Shall we just do the sums here:
Celerity: Flash, alacrity (sup only, only if acting)
Obfuscate: Behind you (sup only - I think)
Protean: form of ghost, Gleam of the red eye (sup only), claws of the dead
(sup only).
Serpentis: Form of the serpent (sup only)
Animalism: aid from bats
Potence: Thrown gate
Thaumaturgy: Movement of the mind (sup only)
Auspex: the spirits touch (sup only. only if blocking)

so there are many cards available, its just a case of making your deck
better - not relying on inferior levels of disciplines.

>Offensive strategies
> --Rush combat: As above, not enough get-in-combat cards.

not true, see above.

> --'Pitch' combat decks: can't put in enough maneuvers or
>enough long-range combat cards to be effective.

Not true, I have made a successful cel/pot/ani deck that did just this

> --Voting: A limited number of damaging vote cards. Especially
>if you want to play Presence voting, rather than Princely vote,
>since you can't use Parity Shift or Sabbat Threat. Presence voting
>also gets hosed because you have only 4 Bewitching Orations and
>4 Bribes, both necessary to help get those votes passed.

Voting is probably more difficult, but there have been four good vote decks
made, all of which are capable of getting a full sweep of victory points
Presence vote is not unworkable, you'll just have to make the most of your
votes and use some praxis siesures, <clan> justicar cards and, especially,
command the Harpies. I made a settite vote deck that was pretty evil. We
also play a house rule for Charming lobby that makes it worth while.

> -- Tap-and-Vote/Bleed. These rely heavily on the combat
>untap cards, Majesty/Earth Meld, to tap out the prey. With
>only four, you can't make it work.

Wrong again. You should also add to this list mummify, freak drive, day
operation, horrid form, form of mist, Force of will, blood bond,
incriminating video tape and change of target (if a stealthy action, ie tap
& vote). and thats with out using the banned Thoughts betrayed and
misdirestion. all of these cards can be used to great effect in a tap and
bleed / vote deck, and with only four wakes, theres no real problem with
anyone waking.

>3. Rare cards become more valuable.
>Since you can only have a limited number of each card, the
>rare stand-ins become much more valuable: Fists of Death
>in place of Torn Signpost and Undead Strength, Kine
>Dominance in place of Govern the Unaligned, etc. This
>favors Mr. Suitcase over the beginning player, a bad thing
>IMO.

I would have to begrudgingly agree with you on this point. Yes it will
favour the player with the most cards, and yes, this is a bad thing. However
everyone in our game group has a very similar amount of cards, and those of
us who have slightly more than the others will often give away cards if
someone requires then for a deck concept.

>4. Because S&B is dominant, everyone ends up playing intercept.
>This slows the game down a lot. Also a bad thing, IMO.

I suppose it would slow the game down, however with no one playing S&B its
not a big problem. We, as a group, enjoy longer games. We are all good
friends and we don't like to see someone sitting out for large lengths of
time, so generally people work to try and keep others in the game, and keep
the game even. we like our games to last a long time so that we can get an
evenings entertainment for free. Well, okay maybe not entirely free, but
even if you spend large amounts of money, its still cheaper than beer, in
the long run.

>Standard responses to CL arguments:
>1. If you have a jerk playing Sneak & Bleed, just
>gang up, or use social pressure to make them quit.
>
>Answer: If you have to resort to the metagame of social
>pressure or ganging up, the game is broken. Most of us
>would rather it worked without having to resort to this.
>And NL/Golden Tenets does.

alternative answer. There is no need to gang up. predator and prey can cope
with an S&B deck quite hapily, given card spread. People who enjoy the game
of Jyhad will *not* enjoy a game with an S&B deck involved in it, even if
they are playing the S&B deck. Therefore the S&B deck is a dead idea. There
is no need to revert to social pressure or ganging up, because the S&B deck
as an idea is avoided like the plague. People who create S&B decks are
usually NL players who want to show everyone how degenerate an S&B deck can
be, and so aren't really in the right mindset to be playing with CLs anyway.
if they continue to play S&B then they themselves will become bored with the
game and either stop playing or build a more fun, more challenging deck.

>2. CL is more creative, because you have to be more inventive
>in combining cards.

also add challenging here.

>Answer: CL shuts off a *lot* of otherwise effective strategies.
>What you're doing is agreeing to play with relatively ineffective
>decks. The game's not broken, so you don't need to do this.
>(As long as you use the Golden Tenets.) Basically, any
>deck you can build under CL you can use under NL. And under
>NL, you don't have to rely on intercept for defense, which
>lets you be more creative, not less.

This is the argument of the unimaginative. there are many ways to create the
deck you want, you just have to use the cards more effectively. if you want
to challenge me feel free. Come up with a deck idea that is plausible in NL
and I reckon that I could make it.

>3. Well, we just play for fun. CL is better for that.
>
>Answer: So do NL players. The range of possible decks
>is much wider under NL.

Not true.

>Voting and rush combat are now workable deck concepts.

As they are under CL

>The games are quicker.

and therefore less fun (In the opinion of our gaming group)

>And you don't have to wean new players off of Sneak & Bleed to
>preserve balance.

Sneak and bleed is boring and not challenging at all. Players will wean
themselves of them of their own accord (as did two of our players, including
myself)

>We'll just have to agree to disagree about which is more fun.

Okay, but you have a lot of preconcieved conceptions of CL games that are
just untrue.

>4. We don't have to worry about broken cards.
>
>Answer: Well, then the game becomes more like Magic --
>whoever draws their broken cards first wins. We don't
>really want that kind of a game, do we? But yes,
>you don't have to worry as much about them.

Actually we do have to worry about broken cards, its just that we have so
few of them: Thoughts betrayed is just outright banned because it has no
counter at all. Misdirection is banned because it is one card that can oust
a player, and has very little in the way of counter - its more of a
voluntary banning as it makes the games boring. we are currently debating
Kiss of Ra and Blood to water, but I think bth of these are probably likely
to stay.

>There have been few broken cards, and they have been
>fixed by errata or the Golden Tenets. Those methods
>are far preferable to the Procrustean bed of Card Limits.

Erratas are erratas and they affect us all, CL or no CL. Golden Tenets or CL
its a simple choice, one that no one can out rightly say that any one is any
better than the other. Both are *Very* slight modifications to the rules of
Jyhad because it doesn't work properly without one of the two. Its just a
matter of personal preference which one you want to use. To say that one is
far preferable to another is just a matter of opinion, and should stay as
such. Personally I prefer CL, you, presumably, prefer the Golden Tenets.

All I can say is that all the arguments that you have placed against Card
Limits are either irrelevant or untrue. I do not wish to grace you with a
reply that tells you everything that is wrong with the NL game, as I haven't
played it in a long time and both my skill level, and that of out playing
group has improved dramatically since then. I would probably get my facts as
wrong as you have about CL. The only thing that I will say is that looking
at the decks that I have seen both printed up on the newsgroup and on
various web pages, I think that our group at least seems to be playing at a
far higher skill level than most of the decks that I have seen. I'm not
saying that all NL players are thick at all, I'm saying that our group is of
a high standard and will have the deck building, and game playing, skill to
work around any problems that other CL players, that you have had experience
in dealing with, may create. I don't want to flame people for playing NL, I
would much rather have people understand that its purely down to personal
choice. I wouldn't like to come out right and say that NL is an inferior to
CL as I don't have enough experience of NL to say it with enough
confidence, and could well end up getting my facts as wrong as you seem to
have. Its not simply a question of NL is good and CL is bad, or vice versa;
its a case of accepting that both games are slightly different, both games
are still Jyhad (or V:tES). When you get down to it theres really only one
fundamental difference; proponents of both variants accept that Jyhad needs
some tweaking from how it is origionally written - the errata half covers
this, but not entirely, therefore some other restrictions are needed the
choice is either to restrict the number of cards that you have available to
you, the othetr is to restrict the viability of certain tactics using the
"golden Tenets" rules modifications. Its all down to personal choice and I
chose CL. If you're not happy with that, fine, just get your facts straight
about the "problems" with CL before you open your mouth



Messages.Author: B.D. Redmond
Messages.Body:
>> Tomb of Ramses III is *****NOT***** too powerful by any means. Lets start
by
>> examining the arguments that claim the contrary.
>

>And let's responding by destroying your own.

well, aren't you a pleasant person! I bet you've got loads of friends!

>> 1: ToR is too powerful because all decks will put on in their deck.
>

>[snipped response to this "arguement"]
>
>Suffice it to say, people aren't saying that ToR is powerful because
>people are putting it in their deck, they _are_ saying that it is too
>powerful, and that people putting it in their deck is a symptom of its
>power. Do note, that useful cards are also put into most decks (Blood
>Dolls, Wakes), though not all, but that the argument was _not_ claiming
>this use = power, but that power = use. (Sorry to be redundant)

If this is the case, why do people post similar arguments for wakes and
blood dolls. people try and change wakes so that they are thaumaturgy cards,
because there is a completely illogical line of thinking that use = power. I
can't understand it myself but there are people out there who believe it to
be true. I think that the mere fact that it is used by everyone balances it.
As for the comments on wakes and blood dolls - any deck that doesn't put in
wakes is really stabbing itself in the foot. no other card is as good at
doing what it does. Other untaps are either played in your action phase,
thereby leaving no room for bluffs, or don't allow you to block as many
different types of actions. Blood dolls possibly aren't as essential - but I
haven't seen a deck yet that does better without them (presumably using some
other way of gaining blood back.

>> 2: ToR is too powerful because it gets you back four blood from the blood
>> bank in the turn it comes out.
>
>> - Okay, perhaps this is a much more reasonable argument, however this
>>blood
>> gain nets at one. How many other ways are there for gaining you one
>>blood?
>> it must be heading towards tripple figures, if not there already.
>

>That's not the full argument. To take this aspect of the argument out of
>context is misleading. The full argument is that it is powerful in its
>own right, but that there is _no_ drawback to its use. The turn it is
>brought out, you can get return on it. Effectively, you pay _ONE_ master
>phase for an ascendance _AND_ its power.

possibly, but then ascendance is pretty cack any way and hardly worth while
using. The card is limiting in the fact that it takes three pool to get out
in the first place, and requires an extra 4 pool to benefit fully, so its
only any good if it turns up early. And I really have to say that under card
limits you really don't have a big problem with this.

>If the card stalled somehow (not usable during the first turn, for
>example), there would be a risk element involved in its use.

okay, possibly, but under CL it very rarely will come out first turn

>As it stands, you can only gain if you have one in a deck (in _nearly_ all
>situations).

Yes. So?

>> 3: Tor is too powerful because it gives you an endless blood supply.
>
>> - So do three other cards, although they are clan specific, they are
>> arguably twice as good. ToR, used as a blood gainer gets back 2 blood
>> every 3 turns for a three blood down payment, the others get you 1 per
>> turn for a 2 pool cost.
>

>This is only if the vampire who has the tomb on it is not used as a
>resource. Assuming a large vampire (say, 10 capacity), a first turn tomb
>of ra nets you 1 pool the first turn, 4 pool the next, and 2 pool the
>last. Effectively, you gain 7 pool over three turns, and get _DOUBLE_
>influence. All for 3 pool.

Yes, but there are two problems with this:
1: the tomb is destroyed when the vampire comes out, therefore
anyone else can then bring out their tomb. Everyone can do this, therfore it
is like saying that everyone starts with 37 pool at the start - it doesn't
really unbalance the game much - make it slightly longer with larger
vampires out possibly, but not unbalanced. who says a slightly more high
powered game wouldn't be more fun anyway?

> Come on! Even if the Tomb is Destroyed, the
> gain made so far is not lost. There needs to be some risk factor.

There is. Sudden reversal. Just the same as any other master card also, a
malky madness deck could use the time auction to steal it with a vote or
Kine Dominance before you've gained the blood for it. Even then, after one
turn its only gained you one and double transfers *ONLY IF YOU ARE PUTTING
BLOOD ONTO VAMPIRES* which I don't see as being hugely powerful. When it
comes down to it, the chances of getting out a location destroyer/stealer
card are probably more likely than getting out the ToR.

>Yes, if used solely in late game as a pool feeder (Tomb on, transfer off),
>it is not as effective as say an Arcane Library, but the fact that it can
>be used for this, as well as the above, makes it too cheap.

if you use it for the above then you *CAN'T* use it as a blood back device,
it either or, not both. just because a card has two effective options
doesn't make it too powerful - I don't see anyone moaning too much about
Kine dominance or govern the unaligned (in a stealthy deck) both of which
have two very useful powers (I mean, they could both gain you 3 pool in a
turn).

thanks for the points. I wouldn't have said you destroyed my arguments, but
I've responded in full to any inclarities you may have pointed out.

thanks

Ben

Even though I have somewhere to be soon, I had to respond to this the
moment I read it...

[Re: Contention that Tomb of Ramses is better than Art Museum, et al.)

>
> Here I think that you will find that you are wrong. If you are going to use
> ToR as a continal blood flow it gives you **less** blood per turn than the
> Art Museum et al (AMea). Lets establish the facts shall we?
> 1: AMea gives you one blood back a turn at the cost of two
> transfers.Surely no one can argue with that?

True, but you still haven't addressed the fact that Tomb of Ra nets you
more effective pool more quickly (effectively matching your transfers for
free), for a much faster effective pool gain. When you start using Tomb
of Ra as a blood machine, it _is_ much slower than the Art Museum, but the
fact that you can use Tomb of Ra for either type makes it superior to Art
Museum, on the whole, though I can't claim it is faster when used as a
pure blood machine.

> There are other reasons why AMea is better than the ToR. They are as
> follows:
> 1: ToR costs three pool to bring out, AMea costs two, thereby
> meaning that AMea cards can be played as a last minute
> defense to gain you the blood to keep you in, where as ToR
> takes longer to reqoup itself back into your pool.

Neither can be played reliably as a last minute defense. The pool loss =

> everyone - there's no challenge to winning with a S&B deck, and it has also

> spread.

Read Judith And Mark's Jyhad page (link available from my page, URL in
.sig). If you can respond to the articles there with any success, maybe

> > -- Rush combat: no longer effective, since you can't put

> wrong. you just have to be clever about it - use more permanent and semi

decks have to play with permanents? A lot of variety, I see.

> > -- Bleed bounce, except for Tremere and Malks, since you
> > can't put enough bounce cards in your deck

> You've got as many as your predator has bleed modifiers, normally.

<boggle>
3 cards (deflection, telepathic misdirection, telepathic counter) equals
_all_ the bleed modifiers... <wink> Okay, whatever you say, pal.

>If not
> its a case of making them count. AI means that no one risks a bleed of three
> or more,

Here's a thought! A broken card to beat a (4CL) broken strategy!

> so telepathic counter becomes useful too. using two clan decks, or
> common secondary skills with skill card bonuses in there makes Toreador and
> ventrue and giovanni readonable - even nosferatu, brujah and gangrel could
> get out one vampire to act as a bleed bouncer.

So the solution for non-Aus/Dom decks is to add Aus/Dom? More variety!!
(?)

>But then, if no one is
> playing S&B, theres no real need for a deck solely devoted to bleed bounce.

And they won't be playing S&B only because you all say "naughty, naughty".

> >Ways of dealing with combat:
> > -- Run-away combat, for clans without celerity.

> I have had many succesful ranged combat decks. Protean is almost as good at
> getting to range, as is thaumaturgy. Fortitude can get you there also (if
> you really need to), as can obfuscate, serpentis, animalism, auspex and
> potence. Its just a case of being prepared and using the cards you have
> available to you to their best capacity. And *then* theres fake out.
> Shall we just do the sums here:
> Celerity: Flash, alacrity (sup only, only if acting)
> Obfuscate: Behind you (sup only - I think)
> Protean: form of ghost, Gleam of the red eye (sup only), claws of the dead
> (sup only).
> Serpentis: Form of the serpent (sup only)
> Animalism: aid from bats
> Potence: Thrown gate
> Thaumaturgy: Movement of the mind (sup only)
> Auspex: the spirits touch (sup only. only if blocking)

> so there are many cards available, its just a case of making your deck
> better - not relying on inferior levels of disciplines.

I see, so somehow its better (and more skillful) to rely on luck to get
those cards into your hand rather than rely on deck construction... The
way it looks above, the only reliable way to get to range is with Protean,
and what are most Gangrel going to be doing at range? Hmm, Aid from Bats
(ooh), Canine Horde (oh!), Body of Sun (eh!), and it only costs them 1
blood to manuever each time.

> >Offensive strategies
> > --Rush combat: As above, not enough get-in-combat cards.
> not true, see above.

Count them.
Not playing with princes: Bum's Rush(temporary/blocked easily), Haven
Uncovered (removable)
Playing with Princes: Archon (removable), Bloodhunt
Playing with Large Non-Camarilla Vampires/Justicar: Covenant of
Blood/variant (both blocked easily/removable)
Playing with Assamites: Contract

Looks to me like the only reliable combat deck would have to be a
permanent based Assamite deck or permanent based Brujah/prince deck. What
if I want a good Gangrel rush? What if I want a brujah-pitch (thrown
objects) deck? A Nossies Assassin deck?

> > --'Pitch' combat decks: can't put in enough maneuvers or
> >enough long-range combat cards to be effective.

> Not true, I have made a successful cel/pot/ani deck that did just this

How many get into combat cards? How many manuevers? (The Kicker) did you
have to equip anything? A pitch deck only uses cards in hand for damage.

> > --Voting: A limited number of damaging vote cards. Especially
> >if you want to play Presence voting, rather than Princely vote,
> >since you can't use Parity Shift or Sabbat Threat. Presence voting
> >also gets hosed because you have only 4 Bewitching Orations and
> >4 Bribes, both necessary to help get those votes passed.

> Voting is probably more difficult, but there have been four good vote decks
> made, all of which are capable of getting a full sweep of victory points
> Presence vote is not unworkable, you'll just have to make the most of your
> votes and use some praxis siesures, <clan> justicar cards and, especially,
> command the Harpies. I made a settite vote deck that was pretty evil. We
> also play a house rule for Charming lobby that makes it worth while.

Still limited compared in that you need to start reaching into the
expensive cards to do it. This gets into the $ aspect of the argument
(good CL decks cost more than good NL decks, and that it costs more $ to
compete in a CL environment).

> > -- Tap-and-Vote/Bleed. These rely heavily on the combat
> >untap cards, Majesty/Earth Meld, to tap out the prey. With
> >only four, you can't make it work.

> Wrong again. You should also add to this list mummify, freak drive, day
> operation, horrid form, form of mist, Force of will, blood bond,
> incriminating video tape and change of target (if a stealthy action, ie tap
> & vote).

Mummify wouldn't work. You'd untap in torpor (and need rescuing), tapping
another minion to minish it up. Blood Bond, incriminating videotape,
change of target, and day operation don't tap out your prey/

> and thats with out using the banned Thoughts betrayed and
> misdirestion. all of these cards can be used to great effect in a tap and
> bleed / vote deck, and with only four wakes, theres no real problem with
> anyone waking.

Misdirection only needs to be banned if WweF isn't reliable.

> >3. Rare cards become more valuable.
> >Since you can only have a limited number of each card, the
> >rare stand-ins become much more valuable: Fists of Death
> >in place of Torn Signpost and Undead Strength, Kine
> >Dominance in place of Govern the Unaligned, etc. This
> >favors Mr. Suitcase over the beginning player, a bad thing
> >IMO.

> I would have to begrudgingly agree with you on this point. Yes it will
> favour the player with the most cards, and yes, this is a bad thing. However
> everyone in our game group has a very similar amount of cards, and those of
> us who have slightly more than the others will often give away cards if
> someone requires then for a deck concept.

What if someone new starts? In NL, they can buy a very limited amount of
cards, trade their rares and be competitve. In CL, they can't (they need
the rares to compete).

> >4. Because S&B is dominant, everyone ends up playing intercept.
> >This slows the game down a lot. Also a bad thing, IMO.

> I suppose it would slow the game down, however with no one playing S&B its
> not a big problem. We, as a group, enjoy longer games. We are all good
> friends and we don't like to see someone sitting out for large lengths of
> time, so generally people work to try and keep others in the game, and keep
> the game even. we like our games to last a long time so that we can get an
> evenings entertainment for free. Well, okay maybe not entirely free, but
> even if you spend large amounts of money, its still cheaper than beer, in
> the long run.

Two continue along this line, the intercept being _necessary_ also limits
variety. Most decks playing intercept also makes it difficult for the
vote decks (above) _and_ rush decks being able to handle S&B (their
attempt at getting equipment is more likely to be blocked).

> >Standard responses to CL arguments:
> >1. If you have a jerk playing Sneak & Bleed, just
> >gang up, or use social pressure to make them quit.

> >Answer: If you have to resort to the metagame of social
> >pressure or ganging up, the game is broken. Most of us
> >would rather it worked without having to resort to this.
> >And NL/Golden Tenets does.

> alternative answer. There is no need to gang up. predator and prey can cope
> with an S&B deck quite hapily, given card spread.

You disagree with yourself above. Which is it? If they can cope, is it
because they are packing anti-Malk S&B?

>People who enjoy the game
> of Jyhad will *not* enjoy a game with an S&B deck involved in it, even if
> they are playing the S&B deck. Therefore the S&B deck is a dead idea.

(Logical fallacy (A !=> B), that aside...)

> There
> is no need to revert to social pressure or ganging up, because the S&B deck
> as an idea is avoided like the plague. People who create S&B decks are
> usually NL players who want to show everyone how degenerate an S&B deck can
> be, and so aren't really in the right mindset to be playing with CLs anyway.

Ah, so you need to avoid making certain deck types that will break the
game to have the game work. I'm confused now, was the S&B deck not a
problem or what?

> if they continue to play S&B then they themselves will become bored with the
> game and either stop playing or build a more fun, more challenging deck.

In NL, there is no need. It is still an easier deck to make, but since
everyone has access to easy defenses against it, the deck creation process
becomes quite intricate.

> >2. CL is more creative, because you have to be more inventive
> >in combining cards.

> also add challenging here.

> >Answer: CL shuts off a *lot* of otherwise effective strategies.
> >What you're doing is agreeing to play with relatively ineffective
> >decks. The game's not broken, so you don't need to do this.
> >(As long as you use the Golden Tenets.) Basically, any
> >deck you can build under CL you can use under NL. And under
> >NL, you don't have to rely on intercept for defense, which
> >lets you be more creative, not less.

> This is the argument of the unimaginative. there are many ways to create the
> deck you want, you just have to use the cards more effectively. if you want
> to challenge me feel free. Come up with a deck idea that is plausible in NL
> and I reckon that I could make it.

Brujah Pitch deck. Good luck. Nossie Assassin deck. Corruption deck.

> >3. Well, we just play for fun. CL is better for that.

> >Answer: So do NL players. The range of possible decks
> >is much wider under NL.

> Not true.

Hmm, seeing as CL is a subset of NL...

The answer to this is usually, well there are non-viable decks in NL that
are viable in CL. However, there are far more possibilities available
that offset those CL stategies that can not compete in the NL environment.

> >Voting and rush combat are now workable deck concepts.

> As they are under CL

See above. The limitations of rush (reliability, necessity of equipment)
are hindered further by the environment (high intercept, no limitation on
S&B)

Vote decks all end up looking mostly alike.

> >The games are quicker.

> and therefore less fun (In the opinion of our gaming group)

Opinion. I like long games (2 to 4 hours), but having _all_ games be long
can make it hard for new people to want to play.

> >And you don't have to wean new players off of Sneak & Bleed to
> >preserve balance.

> Sneak and bleed is boring and not challenging at all. Players will wean
> themselves of them of their own accord (as did two of our players, including
> myself)

See above.

> >We'll just have to agree to disagree about which is more fun.

> Okay, but you have a lot of preconcieved conceptions of CL games that are
> just untrue.

Read Judith and Mark's Jyhad page (link available from my page, URL in
sig.) regarding CL. I have played CL. I have read other people's
accounts of CL. I have converted most people I know from CL. I have
talked to people at game conventions, and when I mention Jyhad they say
"Broken with S&B", until they find out the game wasn't even _designed_ for
CL (standard answer, Neither was Magic. Standard response, but Garfield
made Jyhad after Magic had instituted a CL, and he was aware of the naive
assumptions of limited card supply being false).

> >4. We don't have to worry about broken cards.

> >Answer: Well, then the game becomes more like Magic --
> >whoever draws their broken cards first wins. We don't
> >really want that kind of a game, do we? But yes,
> >you don't have to worry as much about them.

> Actually we do have to worry about broken cards, its just that we have so
> few of them: Thoughts betrayed is just outright banned because it has no
> counter at all. Misdirection is banned because it is one card that can oust
> a player, and has very little in the way of counter - its more of a
> voluntary banning as it makes the games boring. we are currently debating
> Kiss of Ra and Blood to water, but I think bth of these are probably likely
> to stay.

> >There have been few broken cards, and they have been
> >fixed by errata or the Golden Tenets. Those methods
> >are far preferable to the Procrustean bed of Card Limits.

> Erratas are erratas and they affect us all, CL or no CL. Golden Tenets or CL
> its a simple choice, one that no one can out rightly say that any one is any
> better than the other. Both are *Very* slight modifications to the rules of
> Jyhad because it doesn't work properly without one of the two. Its just a
> matter of personal preference which one you want to use. To say that one is
> far preferable to another is just a matter of opinion, and should stay as
> such. Personally I prefer CL, you, presumably, prefer the Golden Tenets.

> All I can say is that all the arguments that you have placed against Card
> Limits are either irrelevant or untrue.

You made no compelling, non-refutable argument regarding CL>

> I do not wish to grace you with a
> reply that tells you everything that is wrong with the NL game, as I haven't
> played it in a long time and both my skill level, and that of out playing
> group has improved dramatically since then. I would probably get my facts as
> wrong as you have about CL. The only thing that I will say is that looking
> at the decks that I have seen both printed up on the newsgroup and on
> various web pages, I think that our group at least seems to be playing at a
> far higher skill level than most of the decks that I have seen.

The web isn't likely a good place to look to determine whether or not a
deck environment is creating good players or no. I publish all submitted
decks (at least, eventually) regardles of how good or bad they are.

> I'm not
> saying that all NL players are thick at all, I'm saying that our group is of
> a high standard and will have the deck building, and game playing, skill to
> work around any problems that other CL players, that you have had experience
> in dealing with, may create. I don't want to flame people for playing NL, I
> would much rather have people understand that its purely down to personal
> choice. I wouldn't like to come out right and say that NL is an inferior to
> CL as I don't have enough experience of NL to say it with enough
> confidence, and could well end up getting my facts as wrong as you seem to
> have. Its not simply a question of NL is good and CL is bad, or vice versa;
> its a case of accepting that both games are slightly different, both games
> are still Jyhad (or V:tES). When you get down to it theres really only one
> fundamental difference; proponents of both variants accept that Jyhad needs
> some tweaking from how it is origionally written - the errata half covers
> this, but not entirely, therefore some other restrictions are needed the
> choice is either to restrict the number of cards that you have available to
> you, the othetr is to restrict the viability of certain tactics using the
> "golden Tenets" rules modifications. Its all down to personal choice and I
> chose CL. If you're not happy with that, fine, just get your facts straight
> about the "problems" with CL before you open your mouth

I have played CL for some time. I think I have gotten my facts straight.
Go back and read what you have written. I think you'll find a lot of
contradictions.

Yes, a CL Jyhad is still roughly the same game... but it has far different
implications than Golden Tenets (now adopted as basicly official). CL
were _never_ meant to have been introduced into Jyhad. One of the Golden
Tenets (vote pushing) can be argued to have been in the original rules
set. The other _is_ now official. CL Jyhad has no real inherent
advantage over NL Jyhad:
- More $ to compete
- Less Variety
- Affected by broken decks
- Now an additional house rule (now that GT are basicly official)
- Not arguable as being a part of design intent (as 1/2 GT are)
- More reliance on luck, less on skill

NL. The way to play.

> >I hope that this will speed the debate up a bit.

Doubtful. I'd like to hear some CL responses that were either a) new, or
b) debateable rather than immediately disprovable.
