On Wed, 9 Oct 1996, B.D. Redmond wrote:

[> I wrote:]

> >And let's responding by destroying your own.

> well, aren't you a pleasant person! I bet you've got loads of friends!

:) I try to be, though I think I was a little heavily caffeinated when I
wrote the above. I apologize for the above statement, it is truly
uncalled for. (As an aside, most people who meet me in person find me
pleasant ;)

> >> 1: ToR is too powerful because all decks will put on in their deck.

[snip]

> >Suffice it to say, people aren't saying that ToR is powerful because
> >people are putting it in their deck, they _are_ saying that it is too
> >powerful, and that people putting it in their deck is a symptom of its
> >power. Do note, that useful cards are also put into most decks (Blood
> >Dolls, Wakes), though not all, but that the argument was _not_ claiming
> >this use = power, but that power = use. (Sorry to be redundant)

> If this is the case, why do people post similar arguments for wakes and
> blood dolls.

Note my claim (above) is not that Dolls or Wakes are under/over powered,
but simply that they are used because they are useful. My claim is that
the above argument really can be ignored. Just because a card is used
does not mean that it is necessarily to powerful, but if a card _is_ too
powerful, people will necessarily put it in if they have access to it.
Thus, use !=> power, and power => use.

> people try and change wakes so that they are thaumaturgy cards,
> because there is a completely illogical line of thinking that use = power. I
> can't understand it myself but there are people out there who believe it to
> be true.

I can agree with this.

>I think that the mere fact that it is used by everyone balances it.

I don't think I can agree with this. If overpowered cards are balanced
because "everyone can use them", the game becomes decided by luck (who
uses it first/more).

> As for the comments on wakes and blood dolls - any deck that doesn't put in
> wakes is really stabbing itself in the foot. no other card is as good at
> doing what it does. Other untaps are either played in your action phase,
> thereby leaving no room for bluffs, or don't allow you to block as many
> different types of actions.

Not true. Many decks don't need wakes because they don't plan on blocking
or they plan on leaving reserves. Other decks don't need wakes because
the other defensive untappers work just fine, or they are only worried
about bleeds in their deck. While I will say that _most_ decks _can_ use
wake at least to marginal benefit, not all need them.

> Blood dolls possibly aren't as essential - but I
> haven't seen a deck yet that does better without them (presumably using some
> other way of gaining blood back.

I have. I had a deck that relied heavily on permanent pool loss for
everyone and defending these cards with vampires. Blood Dolls were
ineffective because it made it easier to take out my defenders. I ended
up using Protracted Investments (not as fast, but takes up less deck
space than Short Term. Also, I used Anson/Rumors of Gehenna/that other
Master Phase booster) and doing quite well with it.

> >> 2: ToR is too powerful because it gets you back four blood from the blood
> >> bank in the turn it comes out.

> >> - Okay, perhaps this is a much more reasonable argument, however this
> >>blood gain nets at one. How many other ways are there for gaining you one
> >>blood? it must be heading towards tripple figures, if not there already.

> >That's not the full argument. To take this aspect of the argument out of
> >context is misleading. The full argument is that it is powerful in its
> >own right, but that there is _no_ drawback to its use. The turn it is
> >brought out, you can get return on it. Effectively, you pay _ONE_ master
> >phase for an ascendance _AND_ its power.

> possibly, but then ascendance is pretty cack any way and hardly worth while
> using.

Again, not really. If you have a deck with a lot of expenses, or you
expect to be on the edge for a long time, Ascendance is good because you
have no pool investment.

> The card is limiting in the fact that it takes three pool to get out
> in the first place, and requires an extra 4 pool to benefit fully, so its
> only any good if it turns up early. And I really have to say that under card
> limits you really don't have a big problem with this.

Having 4 Tomb of Ramses in a 60 card deck gives you a roughly 50% chance
of having it in your opening hand. In a 70 card deck, roughly a 40%
chance, in a 80 card deck, over a third. You were saying?

> >If the card stalled somehow (not usable during the first turn, for
> >example), there would be a risk element involved in its use.

> okay, possibly, but under CL it very rarely will come out first turn

See above. Statistics refute you.

> >As it stands, you can only gain if you have one in a deck (in _nearly_ all
> >situations).

> Yes. So?

There are _very_ few cards where there is win-win, and those that are are
widely regarded as being problematic (evenly if minorly so, as in Wake).
There ought to be risk somewhat proportional to gain, like nearly all the
other card (and _all_ the other definitely balanced cards).

> >> 3: Tor is too powerful because it gives you an endless blood supply.

> >> - So do three other cards, although they are clan specific, they are
> >> arguably twice as good. ToR, used as a blood gainer gets back 2 blood
> >> every 3 turns for a three blood down payment, the others get you 1 per
> >> turn for a 2 pool cost.

> >This is only if the vampire who has the tomb on it is not used as a
> >resource. Assuming a large vampire (say, 10 capacity), a first turn tomb
> >of ra nets you 1 pool the first turn, 4 pool the next, and 2 pool the
> >last. Effectively, you gain 7 pool over three turns, and get _DOUBLE_
> >influence. All for 3 pool.

To clarify my own statement, the tomb need not be out on the first turn.

> Yes, but there are two problems with this:
> 1: the tomb is destroyed when the vampire comes out, therefore
> anyone else can then bring out their tomb. Everyone can do this, therfore it
> is like saying that everyone starts with 37 pool at the start - it doesn't
> really unbalance the game much - make it slightly longer with larger
> vampires out possibly, but not unbalanced. who says a slightly more high
> powered game wouldn't be more fun anyway?

I do. If everyone starts out at higher pool, certain decks (smaller ones,
more combo intensive ones) start to die out. Decks that have risk factors
tend to die out. If everyone has this advantage, the only people that win
out are those that have highly focused pool loss concepts (S&B, Vote),
because their method of damage is so much less card reliant, they can
afford to have everyone have more pool. The combat deck's only chance is
to be _totally_ devastating from the get-go, with no laxity at all.

> > Come on! Even if the Tomb is Destroyed, the
> > gain made so far is not lost. There needs to be some risk factor.

> There is. Sudden reversal.

Where is the risk? Nothing was lost. You caused someone to use a master
phase to edit out your master phase. This is not a risk factor like the
powerbases (which must be protected before there is a return). If Blood
Puppy let you take blood off of it immediately after playing it, it too
would not have a legitimate risk factor (instant returns).

> Just the same as any other master card also, a
> malky madness deck could use the time auction to steal it with a vote

Not legal. You can't use action cards/modifiers with the madness network.

>or
> Kine Dominance before you've gained the blood for it.

Even if legal, they still couldn't do it. Madness Network actions happen
at the end of opponents turn (after influence, after payoff).

> Even then, after one
> turn its only gained you one and double transfers *ONLY IF YOU ARE PUTTING
> BLOOD ONTO VAMPIRES* which I don't see as being hugely powerful. When it
> comes down to it, the chances of getting out a location destroyer/stealer
> card are probably more likely than getting out the ToR.

So, its instant payoff (i.e, no or at best insufficient risk) is balanced
in that it can be destroyed after it has made you gains? So, if
Ascendance was an easily destroyed permanent (Gain 1 stealth each master
phase, destroy as +2 stealth action) would it be balanced?

> >Yes, if used solely in late game as a pool feeder (Tomb on, transfer off),
> >it is not as effective as say an Arcane Library, but the fact that it can
> >be used for this, as well as the above, makes it too cheap.

> if you use it for the above then you *CAN'T* use it as a blood back device,
> it either or, not both.

I was talking about its utility. If you draw it early, you can use it to
bring out vamps. If you draw it mid-late, you can use it to gain pool.

> just because a card has two effective options
> doesn't make it too powerful - I don't see anyone moaning too much about
> Kine dominance or govern the unaligned (in a stealthy deck) both of which
> have two very useful powers (I mean, they could both gain you 3 pool in a
> turn).

Not the same comparison. Tomb of Ra, by itself allows two options. Both
of those cards allow one option conditionally (an inferior dominator) and
another option even more conditionally (a superior dominator). Having 2
options does make any card more powerful comparatively to two cards that
could do one of the two choices. The utility is more. Tomb of Ra is a
single card that acts like either a slightly different Ascendance, _and_ a
slightly stronger Art Museum if used to bring out big vampires, _and_ a
slightly weaker Art Museum if used purely for blood gain, depending on
your needs.

> thanks for the points. I wouldn't have said you destroyed my arguments, but
> I've responded in full to any inclarities you may have pointed out.

I look forward to your next response.

GEN...@leeds.ac.uk (B.D. Redmond) writes:
>>If the card stalled somehow (not usable during the first turn, for
>>example), there would be a risk element involved in its use.

>okay, possibly, but under CL it very rarely will come out first turn

This whole thread is about TOR being in need of a fix.

Your fix (CL) happens to break other cards (Temptation) and destroys
other strategies (Rush combat) and defenses (bleed bounce). But even
if you choose CL, you're still *fixing* (to some extent) the TOR problem.

That doesn't change the fact that the TOR is a problem card as far as
official rules go. TOR is *broken*.

>> Come on! Even if the Tomb is Destroyed, the
>> gain made so far is not lost. There needs to be some risk factor.

>There is. Sudden reversal. Just the same as any other master card also, a

SR is not a risk. You've just traded Master Phase Actions - no net
loss to the person with the TOR.

>malky madness deck could use the time auction to steal it with a vote or

Madness Network is the only risk, and a foreseeable (read, avoidable) one,
at that, as I stated earlier. But thanks for the reminder.

>Kine Dominance before you've gained the blood for it. Even then, after one
>turn its only gained you one and double transfers *ONLY IF YOU ARE PUTTING
>BLOOD ONTO VAMPIRES* which I don't see as being hugely powerful. When it
>comes down to it, the chances of getting out a location destroyer/stealer
>card are probably more likely than getting out the ToR.

And, as always, they will be too late to do any harm (cause net loss) to
the person playing TOR - all costs are recouped in the same turn.

theCorrupter wrote:
>
> Having 4 Tomb of Ramses in a 60 card deck gives you a roughly 50% chance
> of having it in your opening hand. In a 70 card deck, roughly a 40%
> chance, in a 80 card deck, over a third. You were saying?

Man, this probability stuff always amazes me. Even as a math major, I
can never figure the stuff out. Could you explain this? 50% chance of
getting one out of 4 out of 60 seems a little high.

Seems to me like it would be 1 - [Prob. of getting none], which is

N-4 N-5 N-6 N-7 N-8 N-9 N-10
1 - --- * --- * --- * --- * --- * --- * ----
N N-1 N-2 N-3 N-4 N-5 N-6

N-7 N-8 N-9 N-10
= 1 - --- * --- * --- * ----
N N-1 N-2 N-3

= 40% for N = 60
= 31.2% for N = 80

Messages.Author: PDB6
Messages.Body:
B.D. Redmond wrote:
"This is the argument of the unimaginative. there are many ways to create
the deck you want, you just have to use the cards more effectively. if you
want to challenge me feel free. Come up with a deck idea that is plausible
in NL and I reckon that I could make it."

Unimaginitive, huh? I come from a play group that has been playing Jyhad
from its invention, and for the first year and a half, we were staunch 4CL
supporters. After joining onto this news group, I argued every possible
argument you could imagine in favor of 4CL, including every single point
you made, and eventually, after a year and a half of stubornly defending
4CL, we broke down and tried NL/GT (which is now basically DCI rules). We
then realized how absurly wrong we were. If you really want to plat 4CL,
by all means, go ahead, but please stay away from the "You can't handle
4CL beacuse you are dumb" angle.

As for decks I would like to see made under 4CL:
A reliable Gangrel rush deck.
A reliable Nosferatu Potence combat deck.
A reliable Immortal Grapple anti S:CE deck.
A reliable Brujah Thrown Sewer Lid/Gate/Car deck.
A reliable Tremere main line combat deck.
A reliable of any type that uses no disciplines at all.

Granted, one will notice that most of the above decks are combat decks,
which leads one to belive that combat decks are generally unworkable under
4CL. This is because as opposed to Stealth, Intercept, and Dominate Bleed
Bonuses, combat has very little redundancy inherint in its card mix. How
do you make a reliable Potence combat deck with only 4 Undead Strength and
4 Torn Signpost? By getting 4 Fists of Death, which are hard to get
rares, and even that doesn't help that much. How do the Tremere manuver
and/or Press in combat? With 4 Fake Outs and 4 Dead End Alleys? It will
become more of a game of Gin than a game of deck building strategy.

How odes one get into combat under 4CL? Well, there are 4 Bums Rush and 4
Haven Uncovered. The Bums Rushes are just fine, but there are only 4.
The Havens are great, but there are only 4, you can only use 1 per turn,
they can be Sudden Reversaled, they are destroyed easily. That is 8
fairly reliable cards. Blood Hunt requires Princes. That means you need
to be either the Brujah or packed with voteing power. Being packed with
voting power busts up the reliability of the combat deck ("Look. I drew a
Praxis Seizure instead of an Immortal Grapple. Doh."). There is Archon.
It has the same problem. Then there is the "Well, do something that they
NEED to block" angle. Well, if your prey has the choice of blocking the
Rampage on his hunting ground or getting his biggest vamp burned, you kill
a Hunting Ground and keep your hand jamed with combat cards.

By defenition, as 4CL has a smaller possible set of combinations than NL,
there are fewer possible decks under CL, and most of the missing ones are
reliable combat decks. As you are as anti-Malk, as I used to be (when we
played 4CL), I suspect you have never played against the cheesy Malk S+B
deck as a good NL combat deck. The Malks burst like ripe melons, and it
is quite satisfying.

Really? Have you found a better way of gaining pool while at one or two pool yourself?
Immediate gratification means a lot. I wouldn't play with it most of the time, but
dismissing it totally is too much.

And anyway, from a theoretical and game-balance perspective, any card
which duplicates the effect of another card while acheiving another effect at
the same time is overpowered.

> The card is limiting in the fact that it takes three pool to get out
> in the first place, and requires an extra 4 pool to benefit fully,

So you're saying that it only does you any good when you have 7 pool or more?
Gasp, what a restriction. Besides, Tomb's value as a late-game blood-gainer
isn't the issue here; it's the combination of a net blood _gain_ when transferring
with speed, _and_ the option of making it useful later in the game as a resource.

(vide Minion Tap, Hospitality, Minion Tap, Golconda, Redeem the Lost Soul)
it becomes even more abusable.

> so its only any good if it turns up early. And I really have to say that under card
> limits you really don't have a big problem with this.

Bullshit. Speed makes _more_ of a difference in card limits enviroments, especially
when your opponents need to cycle through their deck to get the cards that they need
to deal with you. Info Highways were game-deciders in almost every game that
I played under 4-Cl. I had one; I won. Nathan had one; he won. No one else
ever had Info Highways; they usually lost.

> >If the card stalled somehow (not usable during the first turn, for
> >example), there would be a risk element involved in its use.
>

See the probability thread. With 4 copies in a 60 card deck, one will be in the
opening hand 40% of the time. In 80, it comes to about 32%. That's not
even close to "very rarely".

> >As it stands, you can only gain if you have one in a deck (in _nearly_ all
> >situations).
>
> Yes. So?

Any card which is needed in _all_ decks, or which even gives _most_
decks an advantage for no discernable cost is not a balanced card.
From a theoretical and practical perspective, cards like these
break games.

> >> 3: Tor is too powerful because it gives you an endless blood supply.
> >
> >> - So do three other cards, although they are clan specific, they are
> >> arguably twice as good. ToR, used as a blood gainer gets back 2 blood
> >> every 3 turns for a three blood down payment, the others get you 1 per

> >of ra nets you 1 pool the first turn, 4 pool the next, and 2 pool the
> >last. Effectively, you gain 7 pool over three turns, and get _DOUBLE_
> >influence. All for 3 pool.
>

> Yes, but there are two problems with this:
> 1: the tomb is destroyed when the vampire comes out, therefore
> anyone else can then bring out their tomb.

Not everyone has tombs. Not everyone _should_ want to play with a tomb.
When everyone does want to play with the tomb, because of it's _obvious_
effect on the result of the game, there is something seriously wrong with
the card's balance.

> Everyone can do this, therfore it
> is like saying that everyone starts with 37 pool at the start - it doesn't
> really unbalance the game much -

What if some players don't have tombs? Then they need to spend $$$ to
compete with those who do have tombs... _NO_ card should be necessary
in a balanced game.

> make it slightly longer with larger
> vampires out possibly, but not unbalanced. who says a slightly more high

> powered game wouldn't be more fun anyway?

High powered games being fun? May I refer you to M:tog, in which the "highly
powered" games often involved players dying on the first turn, without any
chance to do anything about it? May I point out that in games which are
"highly powered" the player that gets out the "highly powered" cards almost
invariably wins?

If your idea of fun is having a game be totally randomized due to the position
of a player's "power cards" in their deck, then I suppose that it might be
enjoyable.

> > Come on! Even if the Tomb is Destroyed, the
> > gain made so far is not lost. There needs to be some risk factor.
>
> There is. Sudden reversal.

No loss of pool. No loss of anything. No risk.

> >Yes, if used solely in late game as a pool feeder (Tomb on, transfer off),
> >it is not as effective as say an Arcane Library, but the fact that it can
> >be used for this, as well as the above, makes it too cheap.
>
> if you use it for the above then you *CAN'T* use it as a blood back device,

> it either or, not both. just because a card has two effective options

> doesn't make it too powerful - I don't see anyone moaning too much about
> Kine dominance or govern the unaligned (in a stealthy deck) both of which
> have two very useful powers (I mean, they could both gain you 3 pool in a
> turn).

It's not that you _can_ use it for both at the same time, it's that you
have the option of choosing which usage would be more beneficial to you.
And in the late game, if you don't mind spending a little more time with
the tomb, you can pull out the inner circler for almost free. Hey, that
can happen in the _early_ game too. Imagine what effect _that_ has on
the game.

Or, if you can't imagine it, someone posted a deck which abused Tomb
thoroughly earlier on this thread. Luckily, he supports the idea
that it's unabalanced.

Alec Chang, malkavian gamer.

If you want a more high-powered game, then play with house rules
allowing 6 transfers instead of four, and an extra 7 pool. It's
much fairer than a *rare* card. And, it *is* a different game.

>> Come on! Even if the Tomb is Destroyed, the
>> gain made so far is not lost. There needs to be some risk factor.

The loss of *one* master phase action? Not much of a risk,
compared to the benefit. That's what makes the card unbalanced.

[snip]

Let's revisit the comparison to Arcane Library et. al:

The Arcane Library costs two pool, the Tomb, three.

The Arcane Library gives you one free transfer, and one
free blood a turn.
The Tomb gives you up to four free transfers, and up
to four free blood per turn, but only if you use your
transfers to transfer blood onto a vampire. And the
Tomb will go away after three turns, if you use the
full benefit.

Let's use a little algebra, and directly compare them.
Also put an Ecoterrorists in play along with the Arcane
Library.

The Arcane Library/Ecoterrorist combo
two blood a turn. You transfer two blood onto a vampire,
for a total gain of four blood on your vampires, and
you have 2 transfers left over.
The Library and Ecoterrorists together cost 4 pool.

The Tomb provides two blood a turn, if you transfer
two blood onto a vampire, for a total of four blood
on your vampires. You have two transfers left over.
The Tomb costs 3 pool.

Using the Tomb costs one less Master Phase action, and one less master card.
Using the Tomb costs one less pool.
You *must* transfer blood onto a vampire to get the
benefit from the Tomb.

The Tomb is *almost* equivalent to having two of the most
sought-after cards in the game in play at the same time.

Now compare the Tomb to the Info Highway, at the beginning
of the game:

One good use for the Info Highway is to get vampires out
faster at the beginning of the game.

The Information Highway costs no pool, and gives two
extra transfers a turn.

The Tomb of Ramses provides one extra pool on the first
turn that it is used, and gives four extra transfers.
On subsequent turns, it gives four extra pool, and
four extra transfers. But the Tomb goes away after
3 turns, used like this.

At the beginning of the game, the Tomb is clearly better
than the Information Highway.

In the middle of the game, when you don't want to transfer
a lot of blood out, it is equivalent to having two
Arcane Libraries.

It only starts to fail toward the end of the game, when
you're short on pool and want to mainly be transferring
blood into your pool. And even then, it's OK.
